newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to lock up Hong Kong overstayers.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to lock up Hong Kong overstayers.

text.p: Taiwan has drafted measures to tighten control of visitors from Hong Kong, authorising the jailing of overstayers after rival China takes over the territory on July 1, officials said on Tuesday.
The move aimed to discourage Hong Kong people from streaming into Taiwan when Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, becomes a part of communist China, the officials said.
"Technically, Hong Kong will become part of the mainland from July 1 and there is a need to exercise control on entry and exit by these people," said Taiwan Entry and Exit Bureau official Yin Li-wu.
"Under the Hong Kong and Macau Relations Act, we have been authorised to detain Hong Kong people who overstay or illegal workers from the territory before deporting them," Yin said.
The Portuguese-run enclave of Macau west of Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule in 1999.
About 16,000 Hong Kong and Macau people have applied to the Overseas Chinese Affairs Commission for "overseas Chinese certificates" which are needed to enter Taiwan.

To date there has been no penalty for Hong Kong overstayers because Taiwan regards Hong Kong people as nationals of the exiled Republic of China, rather than Britain, meaning they technically are at home in Taiwan.
Taiwan's top mainland policy planning body, the Mainland Affairs Council, said treatment of illegal Hong Kong immigrants would still be lenient compared to that of those from the mainland.

"Detention will apply to people who cannot afford plane tickets home or are unwilling to leave Taiwan," a council official said. "If they can pay for a plane ticket, they will be deported immediately."
Taiwan, which split from China at the end of a civil war in 1949, incarcerates all illegal immigrants from the mainland regardless of whether they can pay their way home.
To obtain the right to live and work in Taiwan will become more difficult for Hong Kong people after July 1 under regulations recently drafted by the Council of Labour.
Hong Kong people will be required to obtain certificates proving their "overseas Chinese" status and employment letters before being allowed to work in Taiwan, officials said.
There are no restrictions on Hong Kong people working in Taiwan now.
